summary: M5 snapshot budget is now enforced during traversal/preflight instead of only after building the full payload (Issue #88, perf follow-up of #67). The kernel preflights managed context from its known UTF-8 bytes plus a conservative JSON escaping envelope BEFORE variable traversal or json.dumps, and _snapshot_value charges a precise per-value upper bound (raw UTF-8 + escaped quote/backslash/control chars) through a shared _SnappingBudget. Once the estimate exceeds max_bytes the traversal stops and yields the same non-fatal checkpoint_committed=false reason; the final exact length check remains the artifact-cap safeguard.
steps: Verified at 5a1b6e1: _checkpoint_payload detached the whole namespace and JSON-encoded the complete envelope before checking len(payload) > 8MiB, so a 64MiB managed context could allocate the full payload and OOM at the 1GiB ceiling.

Added C-speed exact-size estimation (encode + count quote/backslash/control via delete-translate) so traversal charges an upper bound per string; nested list/dict structural bytes are charged as bounds too.
Preflight rejects only when the estimate is already impossible; a small context still commits (regression) and the user cell never fails because of checkpoint size.

evidence.note: over-budget: result 4096 + checkpoint_committed=false + reason; small context: committed=true

limitations: The work/memory bound is structural (no live OOM benchmark); artifact cap check remains as the final safeguard, so an estimate slightly under the real size can still build once and reject.
